thread.title: Apple Earnings Report Faces Skeptical Wall Street | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Earnings Report Faces Skeptical Wall Street | Investor's Business Daily
text:
After warning of weak iPhone sales in the holiday quarter, Apple ( AAPL ) executives will have some explaining to do when the company releases December-quarter results late Tuesday. Wall Street analysts are likely to pepper executives with tough questions in the Apple earnings conference call.
X On Jan. 2 , Apple preannounced weaker-than-expected sales for its fiscal first quarter ended Dec. 29 . It blamed the revenue shortfall on disappointing iPhone sales, mostly in China. The Cupertino, Calif.-based company slashed its revenue forecast to about $84 billion for the period. Two months earlier, it predicted sales of $89 billion to $93 billion, or $91 billion at the midpoint.
Wall Street now expects Apple earnings of $4.17 a share, up 7% year over year, on sales of $84 billion, down 5%. For the March quarter, analysts see Apple earnings of $2.65 a share, down 3%, on sales of $59.3 billion, down 3%.
Analysts likely will ask executives what Apple plans to do to spur demand for its smartphones. They also will key in on possible growth drivers, such as services, amid softer iPhone sales.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple Earnings Guide Down Possible The company's quarterly earnings report will be the first one where it doesn't provide unit sales for its hardware. Apple wants to shift attention to its ecosystem, including services and accessories. In lieu of hardware unit data, Apple said it will provide profit margins on hardware and services.
Some analysts are bracing for Apple to guide down estimates for its fiscal second quarter ending in March.
Bernstein analyst Toni Sacconaghi thinks a guide down is possible, given reports of high iPhone inventories.
"Consensus Q2 revenues of $59 billion appear appropriately conservative vs. history, but the big question is how much iPhone channel inventory Apple built in Q1, and how much it might draw down in Q2," Sacconaghi said in a report to clients Friday.
Low Bar Set For Apple Stock Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty thinks Apple has a low bar to clear with its December-quarter earnings. In a report Friday, she noted that the bad news is already out of the way.
"IPhones are weak, services growth decelerated and investors are asking what will drive (Apple stock) higher from here," she said. "We believe the recent pullback is an attractive entry point given upcoming services launches and shares already pricing in extremely cautious iPhone replacement cycle and ASP (average selling price) headwinds."
Apple will need to offer a "better than feared" revenue outlook for the stock to get a lift near term, Huberty said.
She expects Apple to launch an over-the-top internet video service in the spring.
Apple stock fell 0.9% to 156.30 on the stock market today .
Editor's Note: This story previously stated that Apple's expected earnings of $4.17 a share represented a drop in earnings. But it represents an increase.
